name: Binomial probability of exactly x VaR exceedances
prompt: What is the probability of observing exactly x VaR exceedances in n days, given the per-day exceedance probability?

variables.meaning: probability of observing exactly x exceedances
total number of observations (days)
number of exceedances
per-day exceedance probability, 1 minus the VaR confidence level (decimal, e.g. 0.05 for 95% VaR)

corruptions.why: The exponents are swapped: p is raised to the number of exceedances x, and (1-p) to the n-x clean days.
Without x! in the denominator you count ordered arrangements, not combinations, and overstate the probability.

sensitivities.why: p(x) rises with p while np is below x and falls once np passes x; it peaks at p = x/n.

intuition: Number of ways to place x bad days among n, times the chance of any one such pattern.

name: Kupiec unconditional coverage likelihood ratio (LR_uc)
prompt: What likelihood-ratio statistic tests whether the observed number of VaR exceedances matches the model's claimed exceedance probability?

variables.meaning: unconditional coverage test statistic; chi-squared with 1 degree of freedom, reject the model above 3.84 at 95%
exceedance probability the model claims, 1 minus the VaR confidence level (decimal)
total number of observations (days)
number of exceedances observed
exceedance rate actually observed

corruptions.why: Signs reversed: the statistic would be negative, because the likelihood at the observed rate x/n is always at least the likelihood at p.
In the model term p must be raised to the number of exceedances x, and (1-p) to the n-x non-exceedance days.

sensitivities.why: LR_uc is zero when x/n equals p and grows as the exceedance count moves away from np in either direction (too many or too few).

intuition: Minus two log of (likelihood under the model's p over likelihood under the observed rate): the further apart, the bigger the statistic.

name: Conditional coverage statistic (LR_cc)

variables.meaning: conditional coverage statistic; chi-squared with 2 degrees of freedom, reject above 5.99 at 95%

independence statistic (chi-squared, 1 degree of freedom; reject independence above 3.84 at 95%)

corruptions.why: The two chi-squared components add; subtracting would let clustering hide a coverage failure.
Without LR_ind the test ignores clustering and is just the unconditional coverage test.

sensitivities.why: A worse exceedance count raises the joint statistic one-for-one.
More evidence of clustering raises the joint statistic one-for-one.

intuition: Coverage plus independence: two one-degree-of-freedom chi-squares make one with two (critical value 5.99).

intuition: KS = the single widest vertical gap between the actual EDF and the perfect uniform line, which is why it can miss tail problems.

name: Cramer-von Mises statistic W^2 for PITs
